patch.value: A declared provenance resolver that fails at runtime is recorded identically to a dimension the harness cannot supply, so a broken probe is invisible until someone reads the source

Established by measurement on 2026-08-03 and generalized from a confirmed instance.

Today a provenance dimension resolves to exactly two observable states in the immutable record: a value, or null. Null is overloaded. It is the correct and permanent encoding for all of the following, which have nothing in common:

- the harness genuinely publishes no such dimension (declared via provenance_unavailable_dimensions, an honest absence)
- no resolver is declared for that dimension on that harness
- a resolver is declared, ran, and failed - wrong path, unreadable file, unparsable content, revoked permission
- probes are disabled by settings or PM_AGENT_PROBES

The confirmed instance: the claude_session_file model resolver computes a session path with an incomplete slug encoding, throws ENOENT, is swallowed by a bare catch, and writes null. The workspace where this happens is this repository. Every mutation it recorded looked exactly like a mutation from a harness that has no model to report. The condition was found by reading the resolver source and recomputing the path by hand, which is not a detection mechanism.

Why the existing instruments do not cover it. summarizeAgentModelProvenance can report per-harness coverage and can set an inert flag when a declared signal produced only unavailable values, but it reads the history corpus after the fact and it is not wired to anything - that gap has its own owner. Even fully wired, it would report 'coverage is zero' without being able to say whether the cause is an unavailable dimension or a broken probe, because the corpus does not carry that distinction. The distinction has to be recorded at write time; it cannot be recovered later from an immutable record that never held it.

This is the instrument-integrity pattern applied one level below where it has been applied before. Prior findings established that a gate which never fails is a hypothesis until you name the input that would fail it. The same argument applies to a resolver: a probe that can only be observed succeeding is a probe nobody can prove broken. The fix is not more probing - it is recording the outcome category of the attempt the runtime already makes.

Privacy boundary: the failure category must be a bounded reason code. Recording the path that failed to open would publish the operator's directory layout into an immutable stream, which the write-time mutation guard exists to prevent.

Scope is the outcome vocabulary and its surfacing. Fixing any individual resolver, and pointing the existing corpus analyzers at real data, are separate owners.

For each declared provenance dimension the runtime distinguishes: resolved, harness-declares-unavailable, resolver-attempted-and-failed, and no-resolver-declared; The failure category records a bounded reason code, never a path or any environment value; pm health surfaces a warning when a declared resolver has a non-zero attempt count and a zero success count in the current workspace; The distinction is observable without reading history: a single bounded command answers 'is my identity provenance working here'; Recording the category costs no additional probe: it is derived from the attempt the runtime already makes
Turns a silent permanent data loss into a diagnosable condition at the moment it starts, rather than after an immutable corpus has already been written without the field.
Resolver health is a first-class, queryable signal: for every declared resolver the workspace can state how many attempts it made, how many resolved, and why the rest did not.

A model resolver shipped, failed on its first real workspace, and wrote a full day of null model attributions before anyone noticed - because null is also the correct value when a harness publishes nothing.
